Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

favour noun and verb

goodwill, approval

also favor, goodwill, good will, win someone’s favour, be in favour with, back in favour, favour someone, back someone, back someone up, kindness, show kindness

classical

Cic. Att. 1.14.7: cum aliquō in grātiam redīre (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.9.3: grātiā et largītiōne … plūrimum poterat

grātia, grātiae f.

noun, first declension

favour, goodwill; one’s standing with others

Both the favour one finds with others and the influence it brings: in grātiā esse cum aliquō, be on good terms with someone; in grātiam redīre, make it up; grātiam inīre ab aliquō, win someone’s favour (Lewis & Short). Its other common senses are a favour done (see favour, a kindness), thanks (grātiās agere) and, in poetry and later prose, charm.

Other words

  • benevolentia, benevolentiae f. — goodwill, kindly feeling

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 20; Amic. 26; Traupman 153, 155

    The goodwill one person feels for another, on which friendship rests; most frequent in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • studium, studiī n. — eager goodwill, devotion to someone

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 5.8.4: eximium et singulāre meum studium (Lewis & Short)

    First zeal, eagerness, and the pursuit or study of something; of persons, devoted support, and so partisanship (Lewis & Short).

  • favor, favōris m. — favour, partiality; popular support

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sest. 115: quī favōre populī tenētur (Lewis & Short); Liv. 2.56.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Rare in Cicero, who apologised for it as a new word, and not in Caesar; frequent from Augustus on, especially of the favour of the people or of a crowd at the games (Lewis & Short).

  • faveō, favēre, fāvī, fautum — favour, be well disposed to, support

    verb, second conjugation, intransitive, + dative · also used · classical · Phaedr. App. 8.8–12: bonīs favēte; Traupman 275

Examples

  • est enim amīcitia nihil aliud nisi omnium dīvīnārum hūmānārumque rērum cum benevolentiā et cāritāte cōnsēnsiō

    for friendship is nothing else than agreement on all things divine and human, with goodwill and affectionCic. Amic. 20

  • amīcōs sublevāte; miserīs parcite; bonīs favēte

    help your friends; spare the wretched; favour the goodPhaedr. App. 8.8–12

  • benevolentiam alicui praestāre

    to show kindness to someoneTraupman 155

See also favour, popular, for, kind.
